disclaimer: aigov is a heuristic scorecard. It is not legal advice, not an audit and not a certification, and it does not attest compliance with any law, regulation or standard. NIST AI RMF functions are used only to organise the report.
headline: Aligned: every evaluated control passes

controls.title: AI usage policy
controls.summary: AI_POLICY.md covers human review, data, approved tools and accountability.
controls.why: Without a written policy, each engineer decides alone which tools to use, what data may be pasted into them and who answers for the output.
controls.remediation: Add AI_POLICY.md (or docs/ai-usage.md) covering mandatory human review, personal and sensitive data, approved tools and accountability.

controls.title: Code ownership
controls.why: CODEOWNERS makes a named person or team responsible for reviewing every change, including generated code.
controls.remediation: Add a CODEOWNERS file (root or .github/) with at least one rule such as `* @org/team`.

controls.title: PR template asks about AI
controls.summary: .github/pull_request_template.md asks about AI assistance and human review.
controls.why: A pull request template turns disclosure of AI assistance and confirmation of human review into a routine step.
controls.remediation: Add .github/pull_request_template.md with a checkbox for AI assistance and one confirming a human reviewed the change.

controls.title: AI provenance is declared and reviewed
controls.summary: 1 file declared as AI-generated or AI-assisted; 0 without a human reviewer.
controls.why: Knowing which files came from an assistant, and who reviewed them, is the basis for every later audit or incident response.
controls.remediation: Declare AI-generated files in .ai-provenance.json or with header markers, and record a human reviewer (reviewed_by) for each.

controls.title: LLM inventory
controls.why: Every LLM provider the product calls receives data. An inventory with purpose and owner makes that data flow visible and accountable.
controls.remediation: List each provider in ai_systems of .ai-provenance.json with provider, purpose, owner and data_categories.

controls.title: Personal data in the repository
controls.summary: No valid CPF or payment card numbers found.
controls.why: Personal data committed to a repository is copied to every clone and may be sent to AI assistants as context.
controls.remediation: Remove real personal data, rewrite history if needed, and use clearly synthetic values in tests and fixtures.

controls.title: Hard-coded secrets
controls.why: Assistants often inline credentials to make examples work. A committed secret must be treated as leaked.
controls.remediation: Revoke and rotate the credential, load it from the environment or a secret manager, and add env files to .gitignore.

controls.title: Risky code patterns
controls.summary: No risky patterns detected outside tests.
controls.why: Generated code frequently reaches for dynamic evaluation, shell calls, unsafe deserialisation or disabled TLS because they are the shortest path to a working demo.
controls.remediation: Replace each pattern with a safe alternative (parameterised SQL, safe_load, argument lists instead of shells, verified TLS) or justify it with a reviewed suppression.

controls.title: Automated tests
controls.summary: 1 test file for 1 source file (ratio 1.00, minimum 0.10).
controls.why: Tests are the cheapest way to check that generated code does what the reviewer believes it does.
controls.remediation: Add tests alongside the code until the test-to-source file ratio reaches min_test_ratio.

controls.title: Human review evidence
controls.summary: 1 of 1 AI-assisted commit has a human Reviewed-by trailer (100%, threshold 80%).
controls.why: A Reviewed-by trailer on AI-assisted commits is durable evidence that a human accepted responsibility for the change.
controls.remediation: Add `Reviewed-by: Name <email>` trailers to AI-assisted commits (for example via your merge tooling) until the rate reaches review_threshold.

controls.title: CI runs tests
controls.why: Continuous integration applies the same checks to every change, whoever or whatever wrote it.
controls.remediation: Add a CI pipeline (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, ...) that runs the test suite on every pull request.

controls.title: Locked dependencies
controls.summary: All 1 dependency manifest are locked or pinned.
controls.why: Assistants suggest packages freely, sometimes ones that do not exist. Locking versions makes every install reviewable and reproducible.
controls.remediation: Commit the lockfile for each package manager, or pin requirements with ==.

controls.title: Security and incident process
controls.why: When generated code causes a vulnerability, people need to know how to report it and who responds.
controls.remediation: Add SECURITY.md describing how to report vulnerabilities and how incidents are handled.

limitations: aigov does not detect AI authorship. It reads what the team declares (manifest, file markers, commit trailers). The absence of signals does not prove that AI was not used.
All checks are heuristics based on file names and regular expressions. Expect false positives and false negatives.
Secret and personal-data detection covers a fixed set of formats (e.g. CPF, payment cards, well-known API key prefixes); other formats are not detected.
Provider detection reads Python, JavaScript/TypeScript and Go imports plus dependency manifests. Other languages are only covered through their dependency manifests.
Comment detection is line-based; multi-line strings and docstrings are scanned as code.
Commit trailers are read anywhere in the commit body, not only in the final paragraph.
Files over the size limit, binary files, symlinks and git-ignored env files are not scanned.
